name: Jean-Jacques Dessalines
role: Haitian revolutionary commander, governor-general and Emperor Jacques I (1804–1806)
summary: Dessalines advocated permanent Haitian independence and the destruction of slavery and colonial proprietorship. His government combined state-administered land and coercive plantation labor with concentrated military authority; he explicitly justified the 1804 massacre of French colonists while seeking unity among Black and mixed-race Haitians.

property-fundamental.rationale: He protected Haitian property while confiscating former French estates and challenging ownership claims for national redistribution.

strong-leader.rationale: He was named governor-general for life and then emperor with sole power to make laws, appoint all officials and decide war and peace; scholarship describes his rule as dictatorial.

state-harmful.rationale: He founded and personally ran a state: Article 1 forms a free, sovereign State and the Empire has ministries, courts and an army under him.

empower-police-military.rationale: He deliberately built a highly militarized state to secure independence.

decide-locally.rationale: His imperial organization made military divisions report directly to the central ruler.

traditional-family.rationale: Article 9 ties worth as a Haitian to being a good father, son and husband, but the constitution and his laws also make marriage purely civil and authorise divorce, including by incompatibility.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: His law confiscates all property formerly held by white French owners for the State and he justified the 1804 reprisals as redress for the crimes of slavery and colonial rule.

gradual-change.rationale: He called on Haitians to strip away the French stamp on laws, habits and towns, and said they had brought the axe to the ancient tree of slavery and prejudices.

free-trade.rationale: Article 22 says commerce knows no fetters and he welcomed neutral traders, yet his decrees bar foreign captains from retail sale, tax imports and exports and set export conditions.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He wished he could fly to the aid of enslaved Martinique and break its fetters, yet Article 36 forbids him to disturb the peace or regime of foreign colonies.

revolution-justified.rationale: He explicitly defends armed revolution to end slavery and French domination.

democracy-best.rationale: His constitution created an empire with no elected body, and his authority rested on a vote of his generals; scholarship calls his governance dictatorial.

right-to-secede.rationale: Article 15 declares the Empire one and indivisible and divides it into military divisions under the emperor.

political-violence-never.rationale: His April proclamation explicitly justifies exterminating French colonists as vengeance and national defense.

separate-church-state.rationale: He deliberately rejected an established religion and public maintenance of clergy.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Article 9 of his constitution holds that no one is worthy to be Haitian unless a good father, son, husband and above all soldier, and the text pairs rights with duties of the citizen.

conscription.rationale: His constitution says no one is worthy of being Haitian unless a good soldier, calls the whole nation to arms at the alarm gun, and his 1806 decree puts coastal captains in state service.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Article 7 makes emigration punishable by death and confiscation of property, and an October 1804 ordinance forbade Haitians to leave the country.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He campaigned to take the Spanish eastern part of the island, which he treated as part of his State and burned in 1805, yet Article 36 of his constitution forbids conquests; the sources pull both ways.

bound-labor.rationale: He personally enforced militarized plantation labor, tying cultivators to estates under military supervision.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: A January 1804 decree pays American captains for each native Black or coloured Haitian they bring home from abroad, where many suffered, so that they can return to their country.

national-self-determination.rationale: He demands permanent independent statehood for Haiti rather than renewed foreign rule.

national-mission.rationale: The declaration warns against a missionary spirit and against posing as lawgiver of the Caribbean, and Article 36 of the 1805 constitution bars conquests or interference in foreign colonies.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His finance and interior minister manages agriculture, commerce, public instruction, prisons, hospitals and roads, and the State holds the confiscated national domain.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: His universal liberation language coexists with explicitly defended collective killing and racially restricted property rights.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Article 4 makes the law one for all, Article 50 admits no dominant religion, and marriage is a purely civil act under government authority.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Despite liberation rhetoric, he demands uncomplaining obedience to laws he says inspiration will dictate.

population-transfer.rationale: He demands removal of the French presence and threatens remaining French-born people with death.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He personally claims responsibility for punitive mass killing, including collective violence beyond battlefield defense.

separated-powers.rationale: His personally pursued imperial design concentrated lawmaking, appointments and executive power.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The constitution has the emperor arrest conspirators for trial by a special council he names and presides over, and allows entry into homes by his order; he ordered the 1804 arrests and killings.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He personally consolidated command of the army and appointment of ministers in the imperial office.

death-penalty.rationale: The 1805 constitution he promulgated says whoever kills his fellow deserves death and has the emperor confirm death sentences; emigration also carries death.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He ties durable independence to preventing the return of colonial ownership.

constituent-assembly.rationale: His constitution was drafted by his generals and sanctioned by him, and revision after his death is left to his council of state rather than an elected assembly.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Article 26 has the emperor designate his own successor in whatever manner he chooses.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Article 30 lets the emperor make and promulgate laws himself, but Article 29 declares a successor who departs from the constitution to be at war with society; the record points both ways.

leader-cult.rationale: The constitution makes the emperor and empress sacred and inviolable and provides national festivals for the emperor and empress, and his coronation was staged as a state ceremony.

land-redistribution.rationale: He confiscated white-owned estates and ended plantation leases, but scholarship says the estates went mainly to the military and the State administered the domain while cultivators stayed on plantations.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Article 3 allows no titles or privileges except those earned by service to liberty, yet Articles 22-27 give his wife, children and successor state salaries and a court.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He rejected any rule over Haiti by another power, swearing to renounce France forever and calling colonial rule tyranny and an inhuman government.

delink-world-market.rationale: He ordered protection for neutral and friendly nations wishing to trade and opened ports to foreign commerce, rather than cutting economic ties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Article 23 says the crown is elective and not hereditary, yet Article 26 lets the emperor name his own successor as he sees fit, so no election among the political nation is described.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The constitution provides no legislature: the emperor makes, seals and promulgates the laws himself.

land-use-tenure.rationale: His land policy vested former colonial estates in the state and administered access through leases.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: He explicitly vows that no European colonist will again enter as proprietor.

non-intervention.rationale: His independence address rejects exporting revolution to neighboring colonies and urges peace with them.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He eliminated rival armed leaders and enforced his authority over resistant cultivators.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: He makes exclusion of European proprietors foundational to Haitian independence.

racial-group-interests.rationale: He urges Black and mixed-race Haitians to unite against European domination.

sacred-nation.rationale: He describes independence as a sacred collective trust demanding sacrifice across generations.

national-church-status.rationale: His religious policy rejected Catholic predominance, leaving worship to individuals.

notes:
One historical inference is marked Inferred. Own independence and massacre proclamations receive priority over labels. The nonintervention answer concerns his stated opposition to exporting revolution, not an assertion that the 1805 eastern campaign never occurred; he treated the remaining French forces there as a threat to independence. The elected, nonhereditary crown does not establish support for hereditary monarchy or dynastic succession. Black national identity included exceptions for naturalized Poles, Germans and women; it does not establish a modern biological-race theory or one-ethnicity nation. Constitutional civil marriage, divorce, family and penal clauses were read but formal sanction alone was not treated as proof of personal advocacy. No specific divorce, religious-dress, apostasy or modern rights position extrapolated from general clauses. No inference from posthumous French indemnity policies. Remaining statements checked across the full documentary collection and scholarly career accounts; ecology and modern technology largely lack evidence.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass. Searched by theme: government, world, liberty, economy, society, means. Answers rest on his declaration, proclamation, 1805 constitution (drafted by his generals but sanctioned and promulgated by the sole ruler; medium confidence, never high), decrees in the 1804-1806 collection, and two scholarly accounts. No inferences. Texts of his private letters were not reachable, and the collection's OCR is rough. Statements on the economy (welfare, minimum wage, taxes), technology, ecology, gender and sexuality had no stated position. His 1805 eastern campaign and the constitution's bar on conquests pull apart, so territorial expansion is 0 at low.
